ProductLineage.description:
The L axis as it appears on a delivered product (INV-CH7-47).

Attributes:
    operators_invoked: The operator set the *producer declares* it ran.
        Declared, not observed — the L6 lineage gate compares it against
        the engine's independent record, and a field the engine filled in
        would make that comparison vacuous.
    policy_bundle_versions: Every Control Plane policy-bundle version bound
        into the state this product was assembled from. A set, because
        state assembled under two bundle versions has two bindings and
        collapsing them would lose the one that mattered.
    graph_snapshot_at: The temporal anchor of the graph state read.
    store_snapshot_pin: The substrate's transaction-time head at the read
        that assembled this product — the
        :class:`~ccf.graph.protocols.StoreSnapshotPin` the reader minted
        once, before its first query — recorded **beside**
        ``graph_snapshot_at`` and never inside it (D-IMPL-88: a store
        transaction counter is not an as-of instant and never implements
        one; ledger row 24.5-L-02; D-IMPL-240). The default,
        :data:`~ccf.graph.protocols.NO_STORE_SNAPSHOT_PIN`, is the positive
        assertion *this product's substrate exposes no native pin* — what
        a SQLite or Postgres deployment is in fact asserting today — and
        it is asserted, never inferred from silence: a product assembled
        before this field existed, and one assembled over a reader that
        cannot pin, both say exactly that. This field is inside
        :func:`~ccf.contracts.canonical.canonical_bytes` by construction
        (every ``model_fields`` member is), so two products differing only
        in pin have different content addresses — which is what makes
        "served at pin N is not reproducible from pin N+1" a property of
        the contract rather than a hope about the replay path.
        Hash-transparent at the sentinel (``D-IMPL-243``): "no pin
        recorded" is what a product assembled before this field
        existed says, so the field is omitted from the canonical form
        at that value; a real pin is rendered and is a new identity.
ProductLineage.title: ProductLineage

StoreSnapshotPin.description:
A store-native transaction pin — the ``"transaction-time"`` axis, as a value.

SDK-defined per CLAUDE.md §11, an extension beside the whitepaper's T axis
(§7.3) and its replay commitment (§7.10): ``D-IMPL-240`` (2) routes the
Fluree pin through this type, and ``D-IMPL-88`` is why the type exists at
all. Its axis is :data:`TemporalAxis` ``"transaction-time"`` and nothing
else: it says *which state of the store* a read saw, never *which
observations* the read admitted.

**Deliberately not a** ``datetime``, and deliberately not an ``int``. A
pin is substrate-shaped — Fluree renders an integer ``t``, a SQL substrate
has no native pin, a content-addressed store might render a digest — and
no arithmetic is ever done on it, so it travels as text. And because it
is a model rather than an instant, :attr:`GraphQuery.as_of` cannot accept
it: pydantic refuses a model where a ``datetime`` is typed, and that
refusal IS the ``D-IMPL-88`` guard at the type level. A caller who tries
to implement the observed-time cut with a transaction counter gets a
validation error at the seam rather than a silently wrong answer.

Attributes:
    substrate: Which store family minted the pin, in the adapter's own
        vocabulary (``ccf.graph.backends.fluree.FLUREE_SUBSTRATE``). A
        reader refuses a pin minted by a different substrate.
    pin: The substrate's rendering of its own head — Fluree's ``t`` as
        decimal text. Opaque to everything outside the adapter that
        minted it.
StoreSnapshotPin.title: StoreSnapshotPin

description:
What crossed a Peering, persisted at the boundary (D-IMPL-58 reading (d)).

SDK-defined extension (CLAUDE.md §7.2, §7.4). Dave's ruling of 2026-07-27
resolves D-IMPL-58 as **reading (d)**: the merged :class:`
~ccf.products.contract.ProductLineage` is persisted *at the admission
boundary* rather than in graph state, and
``ccf.contracts.claims.LineageEntry`` is not extended. The defect being
closed is that :meth:`PeeringAdmissionGate.admit` computed the union into
:attr:`AdmittedProduct.lineage` and nothing read it — ``ingest_admitted``
reads ``admitted.product`` and never ``admitted.lineage`` — so lineage
continuity was a property of a wrapper L2 discards. Under (d) the property
becomes true *and* correctly located: continuity is a property of the
federation boundary, which is what CLAUDE.md §7.2 actually describes.

**Why this is an ArtifactStore artifact and not Control Plane state
(D-IMPL-27).** D-IMPL-27 splits substrates by mutability, and this record is
immutable, versioned and replay-relevant: it describes one crossing that
already happened, so there is nothing about it to update. Content addressing
(D-IMPL-26) then makes immutability structural rather than procedural — the
same bytes yield the same address, so no overwrite path is needed or
offered, and replay resolves an exact version rather than "latest".

**What the audit log does and does not carry — stated here so the next
reader does not repeat the false premise D-IMPL-58's correction paragraph
records.** :meth:`~ccf.controlplane.audit.AuditLog.append` carries *scalars
only* (``action, key, version, resolved, occurred_at, actor,
artifact_class``); there is no payload field, and an
:class:`~ccf.controlplane.audit.AuditEvent` cannot hold a ``ProductLineage``.
So the audit plane answers *was this admitted, by whom, when* — a verdict —
and this artifact answers *what was admitted*. The verdict points at the
record through the reference triple, and neither structure pretends to be
the other.

**Producer and consumer are carried alongside the merge, not only the
merge.** A union that cannot be decomposed cannot be audited: an examiner
handed only ``merged_lineage`` cannot say which side contributed which
operator, and reconstructing it from the peer's product later depends on
that product still being available. All three are recorded so the crossing
is legible from this artifact alone.

Attributes:
    tenant_id: The consuming tenant whose Control Plane admitted (D-IMPL-05).
    peer_id: The peer whose signature and entitlements were verified.
    product_content_address: Address of the admitted product — the bytes
        whose signature verified, which is the same witness the
        attributability gate used. This is what ties the record to a
        specific crossing rather than to a schema.
    producer_lineage: The inbound product's declared lineage.
    consumer_lineage: The consuming fabric's own lineage at admission.
    merged_lineage: The union :func:`union_lineage` computed — what
        CLAUDE.md §7.2's "extends, not replaces" commitment produced.
    admitted_at: The evaluation instant the gate was given. Supplied, never
        read from a clock, so the record is as deterministic as the verdict.

No value here is a deployment's: no peer id, no schema, no regime is
authored in this module (CINV-01).
title: AdmissionRecord
